passages.text: Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole Sanhedrin devised a plan. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests, elders, and scribes met early in the morning.
The whole Sanhedrin joined them.
They made a plan together.
They took Jesus and tied Him up.
They led Jesus away.
They handed Jesus over to Pilate.
passages.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς πρωῒ συμβούλιον ποιήσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον δήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήνεγκαν καὶ παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ

passages.text: So Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate questioned Jesus.
Pilate asked, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
Jesus answered Pilate.
Jesus said, “You say so.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ Πιλᾶτος Σὺ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ λέγει Σὺ λέγεις

passages.text: And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things.
passages.sermon: The chief priests accused Jesus.\r\nThey brought many accusations against Him.
passages.original: Καὶ κατηγόρουν αὐτοῦ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς πολλά

passages.text: Then Pilate questioned Him again, “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to Jesus again.
Pilate asked Jesus a question.
Pilate said, “Will you not answer?”
Pilate said, “See how many charges they bring against you.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος πάλιν ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν λέγων Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν ἴδε πόσα σου κατηγοροῦσιν

passages.text: But to Pilate’s amazement, Jesus made no further reply.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before Pilate.
Pilate was the Roman governor.
The chief priests accused Jesus of many things.
Pilate questioned Jesus.
Jesus did not answer any more.
Pilate was amazed.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίθη ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν Πιλᾶτον

passages.text: Now it was Pilate’s custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate had a custom during the feast.
He released one prisoner to the people at that time.
The people chose which prisoner he would release.
passages.original: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν ἀπέλυεν αὐτοῖς ἕνα δέσμιον ὃν παρῃτοῦντο

passages.text: And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.
passages.sermon:
Barabbas was a man.
People called him Barabbas.
Authorities had put Barabbas in prison.
Barabbas was with other rebels in prison.
These rebels had started an uprising.
During the uprising, the rebels committed murder.
passages.original: ἦν δὲ ὁ λεγόμενος Βαραββᾶς μετὰ τῶν στασιαστῶν δεδεμένος οἵτινες ἐν τῇ στάσει φόνον πεποιήκεισαν

passages.text: So the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
He had a custom during the feast.
He released one prisoner to the people.
The crowd went up to Pilate.
The crowd began to ask Pilate to follow his custom.
passages.original: καὶ ἀναβὰς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρξατο αἰτεῖσθαι καθὼς ἐποίει αὐτοῖς

passages.text: “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?” Pilate asked.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to the crowd.
Pilate asked a question.
He said, “Do you want me to release the King of the Jews to you?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς λέγων Θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν τὸν Βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
The chief priests were Jewish religious leaders.
Pilate knew the chief priests had handed Jesus over to him.
He understood their reason.
The chief priests acted out of envy.
passages.original: ἐγίνωσκεν γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παραδεδώκεισαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς

passages.text: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead.
passages.sermon: The chief priests acted.\r\nThey stirred up the crowd.\r\nThey wanted Pilate to release Barabbas to the people instead of Jesus.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς ἀνέσεισαν τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μᾶλλον τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἀπολύσῃ αὐτοῖς

passages.text: So Pilate asked them again, “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to the people again.
He asked them a question.
He said, “What do you want me to do?”
He referred to Jesus.
He said, “You call Him the King of the Jews.”
He asked, “What should I do with Him?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Τί οὖν θέλετε ποιήσω ὃν λέγετε τὸν Βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: And they shouted back, “Crucify Him!”
passages.sermon: The crowd stood before Pilate.\r\nThe crowd shouted loudly.\r\nThey said, "Crucify Him!"
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ πάλιν ἔκραξαν Σταύρωσον αὐτόν

passages.text: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to the crowd.
Pilate asked them a question.
He said, “Why?”
He said, “What evil has He done?”
The crowd did not answer his question.
The crowd shouted even louder.
They said, “Crucify Him!”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Τί γὰρ ἐποίησεν κακόν Οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραξαν Σταύρωσον αὐτόν

passages.text: And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate wanted to please the crowd.
Pilate released Barabbas to the people.
Pilate ordered Jesus to be flogged.
Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος βουλόμενος τῷ ὄχλῳ τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιῆσαι ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν καὶ παρέδωκεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας ἵνα σταυρωθῇ

passages.text: Then the soldiers led Jesus away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) and called the whole company together.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers took Jesus.
They led Jesus inside the palace.
The palace is called the Praetorium.
The soldiers gathered the whole group of soldiers there.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ στρατιῶται ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν ἔσω τῆς αὐλῆς ὅ ἐστιν Πραιτώριον καὶ συνκαλοῦσιν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν

passages.text: They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers took Jesus.
They put a purple robe on Him.
They made a crown from thorns.
They placed the crown of thorns on His head.
passages.original: καὶ ἐνδιδύσκουσιν αὐτὸν πορφύραν καὶ περιτιθέασιν αὐτῷ πλέξαντες ἀκάνθινον στέφανον

passages.text: And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
passages.sermon: Roman soldiers stood before Jesus.\r\nThey began to salute Him.\r\nThey said, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
passages.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀσπάζεσθαι αὐτόν Χαῖρε Βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: They kept striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they knelt down and bowed before Him.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers surrounded Jesus.
They struck Jesus on the head with a staff.
They spat on Jesus.
They knelt down before Jesus.
They bowed before Him.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔτυπτον αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν καλάμῳ καὶ ἐνέπτυον αὐτῷ καὶ τιθέντες τὰ γόνατα προσεκύνουν αὐτῷ

passages.text: After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers mocked Jesus.
They took off the purple robe from Jesus.
They put Jesus’ own clothes back on Him.
They led Jesus out.
They led Him out to crucify Him.
passages.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν πορφύραν καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἴδια Καὶ ἐξάγουσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα σταυρώσωσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Simon came from Cyrene.
He was the father of Alexander and Rufus.
Simon was passing by.
He was coming in from the country.
The soldiers saw Simon.
They forced Simon to carry the cross of Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀγγαρεύουσιν παράγοντά τινα Σίμωνα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον ἀπ’ ἀγροῦ τὸν πατέρα Ἀλεξάνδρου καὶ Ῥούφου ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.
passages.sermon: The soldiers brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha.\r\nGolgotha means The Place of the Skull.
passages.original: Καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Γολγοθᾶν τόπον ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Κρανίου τόπος

passages.text: There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
passages.sermon: The soldiers offered Jesus wine mixed with myrrh.\r\nJesus did not take the wine.
passages.original: καὶ ἐδίδουν αὐτῷ ἐσμυρνισμένον οἶνον ὃς δὲ οὐκ ἔλαβεν

passages.text: And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.
passages.sermon:
They crucified Jesus.
They took His garments.
They divided His garments among themselves.
They cast lots to decide who would take each piece.
passages.original: Καὶ σταυροῦσιν αὐτὸν καὶ διαμερίζονται τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ βάλλοντες κλῆρον ἐπ’ αὐτὰ τίς τί ἄρῃ

passages.text: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the subject.
Roman soldiers crucified Jesus.
They crucified Him at the third hour of the day.
The third hour means about nine o’clock in the morning.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ ὥρα τρίτη καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν

passages.text: And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
passages.sermon:
The Roman authorities crucified Jesus.
They placed a written charge above Him.
The inscription stated the reason for His execution.
It read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
passages.original: καὶ ἦν ἡ ἐπιγραφὴ τῆς αἰτίας αὐτοῦ ἐπιγεγραμμένη Ο ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ ΤΩΝ ΙΟΥΔΑΙΩΝ

passages.text: Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers crucified Jesus.
They also crucified two robbers with Him.
One robber was on Jesus’ right side.
One robber was on Jesus’ left side.
passages.original: Καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ σταυροῦσιν δύο λῃστάς ἕνα ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ ἕνα ἐξ εὐωνύμων αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, come down from the cross and save Yourself!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was on the cross.
People walked by Him.
These people insulted Jesus.
They shook their heads at Him.
They spoke to Jesus.
They said, “You said you would destroy the temple.
You said you would build it again in three days.
Save yourself now.
Come down from the cross.”
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ λέγοντες Οὐὰ ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ οἰκοδομῶν ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις σῶσον σεαυτὸν καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ

passages.text: In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!
passages.sermon:
The chief priests were present.
The scribes were present.
They mocked Jesus.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “He saved others.
He cannot save Himself.”
passages.original: Ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων ἔλεγον Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι

passages.text: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Christ.
Jesus is the King of Israel.
People spoke to Jesus while He was on the cross.
They said, “Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross.”
They wanted to see Jesus come down from the cross.
They said they would believe if they saw this.
Two men were crucified with Jesus.
These men were on crosses beside Him.
Even these men insulted Jesus.
passages.original: ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ πιστεύσωμεν καὶ οἱ συνεσταυρωμένοι σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν

passages.text: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was on the cross.
The sixth hour came.
Darkness covered all the land.
This darkness lasted until the ninth hour.
passages.original: Καὶ γενομένης ὥρας ἕκτης σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης

passages.text: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus was crucified.
At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out.
He used a loud voice.
He said, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?”
This means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
passages.original: καὶ τῇ ἐνάτῃ ὥρᾳ ἐβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ Ἐλωῒ Ἐλωῒ λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Ὁ Θεός μου ὁ Θεός μου εἰς τί ἐγκατέλιπές με

passages.text: When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.”
passages.sermon:
Some people stood near Jesus.
They heard Jesus cry out.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “Look, He is calling Elijah.”
passages.original: Καί τινες τῶν παρεστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον Ἴδε Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ

passages.text: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
passages.sermon:
A man ran to Jesus.
He took a sponge.
He filled the sponge with sour wine.
He put the sponge on a reed.
He held the sponge up to Jesus to drink.
He said, “Leave Him alone.”
He said, “Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
passages.original: Δραμὼν δέ τις καὶ γεμίσας σπόγγον ὄξους περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν λέγων Ἄφετε ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας καθελεῖν αὐτόν

passages.text: But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was on the cross.
He let out a loud cry.
He breathed His last breath.
Jesus died.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀφεὶς φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐξέπνευσεν

passages.text: And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
passages.sermon:
The veil hung inside the temple.
The veil separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
The veil was very large and thick.
The veil was important in Jewish worship.
God tore the veil in two pieces.
The tear started at the top and went down to the bottom.
No person tore the veil.
God showed His power by tearing the veil.
The veil was now open from top to bottom.
passages.original: Καὶ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη εἰς δύο ἀπ’ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω

passages.text: When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
passages.sermon:
A Roman centurion stood in front of Jesus.
The centurion watched Jesus die.
Jesus breathed His last breath.
The centurion saw how Jesus died.
The centurion spoke.
He said, “Truly, this man was the Son of God.”
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ κεντυρίων ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐξ ἐναντίας αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὕτως ἐξέπνευσεν εἶπεν Ἀληθῶς οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος Υἱὸς Θεοῦ ἦν

passages.text: And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
passages.sermon:
There were women watching from a distance.
Mary Magdalene was one of these women.
Mary, the mother of James the younger and of Joses, was also there.
Salome was there too.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δὲ καὶ γυναῖκες ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι ἐν αἷς καὶ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου τοῦ μικροῦ καὶ Ἰωσῆτος μήτηρ καὶ Σαλώμη

passages.text: These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him.
passages.sermon: These women followed Jesus in Galilee.\r\nThese women served Jesus in Galilee.\r\nMany other women also traveled with Jesus to Jerusalem.
passages.original: αἳ ὅτε ἦν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ καὶ ἄλλαι πολλαὶ αἱ συναναβᾶσαι αὐτῷ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα

passages.text: Now it was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath), Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
It was evening.
This day was called Preparation Day.
Preparation Day is the day before the Sabbath.
Joseph came from Arimathea.
Joseph was a respected member of the Council.
Joseph was waiting for the kingdom of God.
Joseph acted with courage.
Joseph went to Pilate.
Joseph asked Pilate for the body of Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤδη ὀψίας γενομένης ἐπεὶ ἦν Παρασκευή ὅ ἐστιν προσάββατον ἐλθὼν Ἰωσὴφ ὁ ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας εὐσχήμων βουλευτής ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν προσδεχόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς τὸν Πιλᾶτον καὶ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate heard that Jesus was already dead.
Pilate felt surprised.
Pilate called for the centurion.
Pilate asked the centurion if Jesus had died earlier.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἐθαύμασεν εἰ ἤδη τέθνηκεν καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν κεντυρίωνα ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν εἰ πάλαι ἀπέθανεν

passages.text: When Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
A centurion was a Roman officer.
Pilate wanted to know if Jesus was really dead.
The centurion told Pilate that Jesus was dead.
Pilate learned the truth from the centurion.
Pilate gave the body of Jesus to Joseph.
passages.original: καὶ γνοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ κεντυρίωνος ἐδωρήσατο τὸ πτῶμα τῷ Ἰωσήφ

passages.text: So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a follower of Jesus.
Joseph bought a linen cloth.
Joseph took down the body of Jesus.
Joseph wrapped the body of Jesus in the linen cloth.
Joseph placed the body of Jesus in a tomb.
The tomb had been cut out of rock.
Joseph rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀγοράσας σινδόνα καθελὼν αὐτὸν ἐνείλησεν τῇ σινδόνι καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνημείῳ ὃ ἦν λελατομημένον ἐκ πέτρας καὶ προσεκύλισεν λίθον ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν τοῦ μνημείου

passages.text: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph saw where His body was placed.
passages.sermon: Mary Magdalene was a follower of Jesus.\r\nMary, the mother of Joseph, was also present.\r\nBoth women saw the place where the body of Jesus was laid.
passages.original: ἡ δὲ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰωσῆτος ἐθεώρουν ποῦ τέθειται
